Initial assessment: The prompt describes a rebuild of the visual layer and data visualization components. The user has provided screenshots of the current application state across several views, likely for comparison during the rebuild. Analyzing the images is the first step.

The screenshots appear to represent distinct views of an application dealing with data intake, entities, attribution, and risk. Examining each for UI elements, data presentation styles, and overall layout will establish a baseline for the rebuild. This baseline will inform the design choices for the new visual layer.


Analyzing the provided screenshots against the rebuild mandate. The "5-Second Test," "Wow Test," and "Fit Test" criteria are the primary evaluation metrics. Considering each of the six views as the mandate specifies.


The rebuild requires creating reusable components for all six views. Defined components include `KpiTile`, `StoryBanner`, `SectionCard`, `ScaleBar`, `RadialGauge`, `VerdictChip`, `EvidenceChip`, `GlossaryTerm`, `LinkLayer`, and `TimelineStrip`. Each component must adhere to specific visual and functional requirements. These components will be built within a shared kit to ensure consistency and efficient reuse across the application.


The application's architecture includes a global shell with left rail navigation and a header containing interactive elements like a case clock and mutator dropdown. Each view, starting with the network view, features specific components such as a multi-layer actor topology graph and a support panel displaying device information and exposure data. These are the main structural components within each view.

A Dinic Min-Cut Freeze Budget visualization was also identified, along with a support panel showcasing dual containment and recovery waterfall charts. The attribution view features a "Haystack -> Needle" subscriber canvas with interactive elements and a SIM-swap precursor timeline.
